answer.rationale: The two metrics actually degrading are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and those are causally linked: onboarding completion is upstream of first meaningful action. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifted first-week activation) both point at this lever, so I verify those two — they are the memories I would actually be spending the slot on, and their original records will tell me whether the lift was measured on a comparable self-serve SMB cohort and whether it persisted past week one or was just a funnel-shape artifact. I deliberately do NOT spend the slot on promotional_pricing even though the competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal: memory_73 already records the decisive detail, that the +31% signups / +18% revenue came from price-sensitive cohorts with early retention -12pp under fixed acquisition channels. Against a stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a known value-destroying trade dressed as a growth win, and matching a competitor on price would additionally select for exactly the cohort that churned. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are both credible but neither addresses the deterioration in front of us, and referral requires an established base that a weakening activation funnel is not currently replenishing. Uncertainty I am holding rather than resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, and consolidation strips the conditions under which a result held — memory_86 and memory_31 may describe the same underlying experiment double-counted, and both predate the current competitive environment by 35-45 days, so a lift measured then may not reproduce now.
